name: fix_fastapi_duplicate_email
description: Enforces unique email across a repository check and a 409 in the router
prompts: Registration should reject duplicate email addresses, but two layers are broken: UserRepository.email_exists in app/repository.py always returns False, and create_user in app/routers/users.py never checks it. Fix BOTH: make email_exists correctly report whether an email is already registered, and have create_user raise HTTP 409 (Conflict) with a JSON error when the email is taken, before adding. A first registration for an email returns 201; a second with the same email returns 409 and does not create a second user. Different emails still work.

setup_files.app/schemas.py:
from pydantic import BaseModel


class UserCreate(BaseModel):
    username: str
    email: str


class UserOut(BaseModel):
    id: int
    username: str
    email: str
setup_files.app/main.py:
from fastapi import FastAPI

from app.routers import users

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(users.router)

test_setup_files.test_dup.py:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

r = client.post("/users", json={"username": "ada", "email": "a@x.io"})
assert r.status_code == 201, r.text
assert r.json()["id"] == 1, r.json()

# same email -> 409, and it must NOT consume an id (nothing added)
r = client.post("/users", json={"username": "ada2", "email": "a@x.io"})
assert r.status_code == 409, f"duplicate email must be 409, got {r.status_code} {r.text}"

# a different email still works and gets the NEXT id (2), proving the
# rejected duplicate created nothing
r = client.post("/users", json={"username": "bob", "email": "b@x.io"})
assert r.status_code == 201, r.text
assert r.json()["id"] == 2, f"the rejected duplicate consumed an id: bob got {r.json()['id']}, want 2"
print("PASS")

files.app/routers/users.py:
from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException

from app import schemas
from app.repository import UserRepository

router = APIRouter()
repo = UserRepository()


@router.post("/users", response_model=schemas.UserOut, status_code=201)
def create_user(payload: schemas.UserCreate):
    user = repo.add(payload.username, payload.email)
    if repo.email_exists(payload.email) and sum(
        1 for u in repo.list() if u["email"] == payload.email) > 1:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="email already registered")
    return user
